source_name: FAÚ — Národní strategie pro boj proti praní špinavých peněz a financování terorismu (2025–2027)
why_relevant: Government-level AML/CFT strategy naming planned legislative changes, supervisory priorities and timelines for the coming period — a forward-looking deadline and regulation pipeline for banks and PSPs.

source_name: FAÚ — Oznámení o podezřelém obchodu (STR reporting) + electronic applications (MoneyWeb / MoneyWeb Lite, e-formulář)
why_relevant: Defines the operational reporting channel and format obliged entities must use under § 18–19 AMLZ: MoneyWeb (VPN + cooperation agreement), MoneyWeb Lite desktop client, electronic form, datová schránka. Changes here are direct integration requirements for bank/PSP compliance systems, and the reporting timing rules carry the hard deadlines.

source_name: FAÚ — Dozorová činnost (supervisory activity section)
why_relevant: Describes FAÚ's inspection powers and process over all ~30 categories of obliged entities and, for financial-sector entities, the shared supervision arrangement with ČNB. Useful for mapping which authority actually inspects a given bank or payment institution.

source_name: FAÚ English-language site (FIU Czech Republic)
why_relevant: Parallel EN tree carrying selected guidance in English (e.g. MP č. 9 kontrola klienta EN version) and international agenda pages (MONEYVAL, Egmont). Valuable for cross-border banking groups and for entity matching against EN-language sources; note EN coverage lags the cs tree.

source_name: FAÚ legacy archive site (archiv.financnianalytickyurad.cz)
why_relevant: Archived pre-migration FAÚ content (elektronická komunikace, older OPO pages, superseded guidance). Essential for reconstructing the historical obligation timeline when current pages have been silently rewritten.

source_name: MZV ČR — Vnitrostátní sankční seznam (Czech national sanctions list, Act 1/2023 Sb.)
why_relevant: The national sanctions list is maintained and published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (not FAÚ), while FAÚ supervises whether obliged entities screen against it. Payment onboarding and screening engines must ingest this list alongside EU/UN lists — it is the CZ-specific screening feed.

source_name: data.gov.cz (NKOD) — Vnitrostátní sankční seznam open dataset
why_relevant: Machine-readable (CSV) distribution of the Czech national sanctions list via the national open data catalogue — the correct ingestion path for automated screening rather than page scraping. NKOD is also a pointer to other AML-adjacent official datasets.

source_name: ČNB — AML/CFT supervision, dohledové benchmarky and stanoviska k regulaci finančního trhu
why_relevant: Boundary source for this cell: ČNB supervises AML/CFT of banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions under § 35 AMLZ jointly with FAÚ, and publishes its AML/CFT supervisory strategy (2023–2026), dohledové benchmarky and RS-numbered opinions that interpret AMLZ for PSPs. Tracking FAÚ without ČNB leaves half the obligation stream invisible — though it belongs primarily to a different coverage cell, the AML overlap must be linked.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — AML legislation owner (zákon č. 253/2008 Sb. and its novely)
why_relevant: MF is the ministry that drafts AMLZ amendments (transposition of AMLD5/AMLD6 and adaptation to the EU AML package/AMLR). MF pages carry draft bills, důvodové zprávy and consultation material before the obligations become law — the earliest reliable signal of upcoming obligations for payment institutions.

source_name: zakonyprolidi.cz — consolidated text of zákon č. 253/2008 Sb. and related acts, with explanatory memoranda
why_relevant: Practical consolidated-text and amendment-history source for AMLZ, 69/2006 Sb. and 1/2023 Sb., including hosted důvodové zprávy PDFs. Useful for pinning exact effective dates of obligations and deadlines; a commercial aggregator, so treat as convenience layer over e-Sbírka rather than the legal authority.

source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) — Czech Republic evaluation and follow-up reports
why_relevant: Independent external assessment of Czech AML/CFT effectiveness and technical compliance. Czechia has been in enhanced follow-up since the 2018 MER, with targeted financial sanctions, virtual assets and cash couriers persistently rated partially compliant — these ratings reliably predict the next round of domestic legislative and supervisory tightening affecting banks and PSPs.

source_name: AMLA — EU Authority for Anti-Money Laundering (consultations and RTS)
why_relevant: Operational since 1 July 2025, AMLA issues the RTS/guidelines under the EU AML package (AMLR/AMLD6) that will progressively displace national metodické pokyny for banks and PSPs, and runs public consultations (e.g. Feb 2026 draft RTS on customer due diligence). Deadline stream for the CZ market even though the issuer is not Czech.

source_name: AML solutions (amlsolutions.cz) — Czech AML practitioner news and deadline alerts
why_relevant: Commercial Czech AML compliance vendor whose aktuality reliably surface FAÚ deadline events in plain language (e.g. the kontaktní osoba notification deadline, new MP č. 6 for the gambling sector, high-risk country list changes) often faster and more legibly than the FAÚ page itself. Useful as an early-warning tripwire, never as the authority.

source_name: gdpr.cz / compliance-portal reporting on FAÚ annual report fines
why_relevant: Secondary summaries that extract the enforcement/fine statistics out of FAÚ annual reports shortly after publication. Useful as a cross-check and as a discovery signal that a new výroční zpráva has landed; the underlying FAÚ PDF remains authoritative.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů (official site)
why_relevant: Czech data protection authority; sole national publisher of GDPR inspection outcomes, sanctions and methodological opinions that bind banks and PSPs (client data security, automated decision-making, credit registers, biometric onboarding).

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Ukončené kontroly (completed inspections archive, by year and sector)
why_relevant: Year-by-year inspection archive with explicit banking/finance sector entries (e.g. 'Bankovní sektor', 'Bankovní a finanční sektor'); best structured evidence of how GDPR enforcement lands on banks.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Protokoly o kontrole / poskytnuté informace (inspection protocols released under FOI)
why_relevant: Full-text inspection protocols (čj. UOOU-xxxxx) released via the Act 106/1999 FOI channel expose the actual control questions, findings and remedies applied to regulated entities — far richer than press summaries.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Výroční zpráva (annual report)
why_relevant: Annual statutory report gives enforcement volumes (inspections opened/closed, administrative proceedings, fines) and signals the next year's control plan priorities — a leading indicator of where bank inspections go next.

source_name: NÚKIB – Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost (official site)
why_relevant: Czech cybersecurity authority and NIS2 transposition regulator; publishes the new ZKB regime, implementing decrees, methodologies, threat warnings and reporting duties that now bind banks, PSPs and their ICT suppliers.

source_name: NÚKIB – Aktuality: publication of the new Cybersecurity Act (zák. č. 264/2025 Sb.)
why_relevant: Authoritative announcement of the NIS2 transposition act effective 1 Nov 2025 — the anchor document for every downstream registration and implementation deadline for financial entities.

source_name: Portál NÚKIB (regulated-service notification portal, calculator, decree explanatory memoranda)
why_relevant: Operational portal where regulated services must be notified ('ohlášení regulované služby'); hosts the scope calculator and decree documents (e.g. vyhláška č. 408/2025 Sb. o regulovaných službách) that determine whether a bank/PSP falls in the higher or lower regime and by when.

source_name: Osvěta NÚKIB (NÚKIB e-learning / awareness platform, NIS2 course modules)
why_relevant: Regulator's own training modules spell out, in plain language, who is in scope and the notification/communication mechanics — useful for interpreting obligations and deadlines without legal ambiguity.

source_name: ÚOHS – Platební styk (payment systems department, interchange/IFR supervision)
why_relevant: Confirms ÚOHS is the Czech supervisor for Regulation (EU) 2015/751 (interchange fees) since 13 Jan 2017 — covering territorial licence restrictions, scheme/processing separation, non-discrimination and cross-subsidy bans. Directly shapes card economics for issuers/acquirers.

source_name: ÚOHS – Tiskové zprávy: hospodářská soutěž (competition press releases)
why_relevant: Fastest public signal of competition/payment-market interventions, fines and sector opinions; includes bank-service assessments (e.g. 'vklad na kartu') and a data-protection-and-competition information sheet showing convergence of the two regimes.

source_name: ÚOHS – Sborníky rozhodnutí (collected decisions)
why_relevant: ÚOHS's curated decision collections; the entry point for tracing decision practice, though the observed collection page sits under the public-procurement methodology branch — competition/payment decisions likely need the separate decision database.

source_name: ÚOHS – Výroční zpráva (annual report, enforcement statistics)
why_relevant: Annual enforcement totals and priority setting for the competition authority, including where payment/financial markets sit in its agenda.
